Winter Solstice Citrus Preserves

Served at: Winter Solstice (Yule)

Approximately 4-5 (8 ounce / 240 ml) jarsPrep 30 min active, plus 12-18 hours soakingCook 1.5-2 hours

These bright, tangy citrus preserves are a wonderful way to celebrate the Winter Solstice, bringing a burst of sunshine and warmth to the darkest days of the year. Made with seasonal citrus, they symbolize the return of light and the preservation of nature's bounty, perfect for spreading on toast or gifting during Yule festivities.

Ingredients

  • 2 large navel oranges (about 1.5 pounds / 680 g)
  • 2 large lemons (about 1 pound / 450 g)
  • 6 cups (1.4 liters) water, plus more for soaking
  • 6 cups (1.2 kg) granulated sugar

Method

  1. Thoroughly wash the oranges and lemons. Slice off the ends of each fruit.
  2. Cut the fruit in half lengthwise, then slice each half into very thin crescent moons (about 1/8 inch / 3 mm thick). Remove any large seeds and reserve them. You can also remove the central pith if desired, but it contains pectin.
  3. Place the sliced fruit (peel, pulp, and juice) into a large, non-reactive pot or bowl. Tie the reserved seeds and any extra pith in a piece of cheesecloth to create a 'pectin bag'. Add this bag to the pot.
  4. Pour 6 cups (1.4 liters) of water over the fruit. Cover the pot and let it soak at room temperature for 12-18 hours, or overnight. This step softens the peels and helps extract pectin.
  5. After soaking, place the pot with the fruit and pectin bag on the stove over medium-high heat. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, or until the citrus peels are very tender and translucent.
  6. Remove the pectin bag from the pot, squeezing it well with a spoon against the side of the pot to extract all the liquid and pectin before discarding the bag.
  7. Add the granulated sugar to the pot. Stir constantly over medium heat until the sugar is completely dissolved. Increase the heat to high and bring the mixture to a rolling boil. Do not stir once it starts boiling rapidly.
  8. Boil rapidly for 20-40 minutes, or until the preserves reach the setting point. To test for set, place a small spoonful of preserves on a chilled plate, let it cool for a minute, then push it with your finger. If it wrinkles, it's ready. Alternatively, use a candy thermometer; it should reach 220°F (104°C).
  9. Remove the pot from the heat. Skim off any foam from the surface with a spoon. Let the preserves cool for 5-10 minutes to allow the fruit to distribute evenly.
  10. Meanwhile, sterilize your canning jars and lids according to manufacturer's instructions. Ladle the hot preserves into the sterilized jars, leaving 1/4 inch (6 mm) headspace.
  11. Wipe the rims clean, place lids on top, and screw on the bands until finger-tight. Process in a boiling water canner for 10 minutes (adjusting for altitude if necessary) to ensure a vacuum seal and shelf stability.
  12. Carefully remove jars from the canner and place them on a towel-lined counter to cool completely. Check seals after 12-24 hours; lids should be concave and not flex when pressed.

Tips

  • For a spicier preserve, add a cinnamon stick or a few cloves to the pectin bag during the simmering stage, removing them before adding sugar.
  • Ensure your pot is large enough to accommodate the rapid boiling; it will bubble up significantly.
  • Store sealed jars in a cool, dark place for up to a year. Once opened, refrigerate and consume within 2-3 weeks.
